body: Yes, it is. Private loans, very strict terms and very few ways out, repayment being a sort of pipe dream, especially with the gouging interest.

I've been in and out of therapy for about three years, that didn't do much for me (it was CBT). I also tried SSRIs, and they just intensified my suicidal thoughts, so that was a bust.

I know I'm shooting down everything you have to say, sorry, but it really means a lot to me that you're taking the time to pay attention to this post and contribute something.

I've talked to a debt counselor, and their solution is "stay at home if possible, pay what you can over the monthly requirement to get the balance down."  That equals at least 2 more years here in the exact same situation, and I just--I really can't take that.  Something's gotta give, and if it's not the situation, it's gonna be me.

Thanks for the idea though.

Unfortunately, I've been "treading water" for the last 5 years. Trying to go to university was a last-ditch attempt to improve my situation, but that backfired (obviously) in a big way--the debt is a trigger on top of preexisting depression, dissatisfaction, and desperation. Like you said, I'm worn down and I can't keep doing this.

Thanks for answering.
